ca_manx_boulders_northwest_face.blurb: A compact set of eleven boulder problems on the northwest side of the Manx Boulders, a pair of oblong blocks tucked behind Cyclops Rock in the Hidden Valley part of Joshua Tree National Park. Grades start at VB and top out at V4, with most problems falling between V0 and V3, so beginners and intermediates both get a good session. Landings are generally flat, the surroundings are open and sandy, and the short walk keeps it popular, so expect company. Bring pads and a spotter for the higher lip moves.
ca_manx_boulders_northwest_face.approach: Follow the well-used trail past the south end of Cyclops Rock to its back side; the boulders stand just beyond in an open, sandy flat.

ca_dancing_outlaw_boulder.blurb: One boulder within the Brickyard, a shaded sandstone bouldering area in the hills above Santa Barbara. Its eleven problems lean hard: a couple of V3 and V4 lines to warm up on, then a cluster running from V8 up to V10. The steep north side carries the headline lines, with powerful moves on slopers, crimps and undercling-style holds and a fair amount of height on the harder ones. Plan on several pads and a spotter. The walk in from the road is a short downhill stroll.

ca_flower_pot_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of short boulders in the Central Basin of Boulder Basin, on Black Mountain in the San Jacinto Mountains above Idyllwild, at roughly 7,500 feet among pines. The eleven problems are mostly friendly: VB through V2 for nearly all of them, with a single V6 standing well apart. That makes it a good spot for beginners, warm-ups and families, while the wider Black Mountain area has much taller and stiffer problems nearby. At this elevation it is mainly a summer and fall destination.

ca_mill_creek_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder standing alone in the brush beside Highway 38 in the Mill Creek canyon, on the road between Mentone and Big Bear in the San Bernardino Mountains. It holds eleven problems from V0 to V4, with plenty of easy options for beginners and the tougher lines on the west and south sides. A short walk of about five minutes from the roadside turnout makes it a quick stop rather than a full day out, so bring a couple of pads.

ca_dream_street.blurb: A steeply overhanging wall about forty feet tall inside Echo Cliffs, the big sport-climbing venue of the Santa Monica Mountains northwest of Los Angeles. Eleven bolted routes, all 5.12 or harder: five at 5.12, five at 5.13 and one at 5.14. They are shorter than most routes at Echo Cliffs but very powerful, on blue-gray rock with pockets and blocky holds. The wall sits in shade early in the day and again from mid-afternoon on. This is a destination for strong sport climbers, not a place to learn.

ca_northern_formation_the.blurb: A small outcrop near the summit of Mount Tamalpais in Mount Tamalpais State Park, above Mill Valley in Marin County. Eleven routes mix top-rope and trad, mostly easy to moderate between 5.4 and 5.8, with one 5.10. Most parties rig top ropes from natural anchors, so long slings and a few cams are handy. The formation is easy to miss on a first visit. The real draw is the view across the Bay Area, which is hard to beat for a cragging day, and the gentle grades suit newer climbers.
